# A node's `#id` names the instance its argument list is building, so an
# argument of that list may not read it. The checker says so, with a position.
#
# This file used to pin the opposite: the fold's re-entry guard left such a
# prop standing and html wrote no <title> for it, silently, which CLAUDE.md
# recorded as the survivable answer rather than the right one. This is the
# right one for the half a node's id covers. `const a int = a` is the same
# shape one layer down and is a scope of its own, still accepted by `sngl
# check` and still guarded in consteval (const_reads_itself.txt).
! sngl check selfref.sngl
stderr 'names the node this argument list declares'
! sngl generate --lang none --platform html --out out selfref.sngl

# Mutual reference between two pages is refused too, by the lowering that
# answers a read of a node's prop (passNodePropReads): each title is the other,
# so neither has an answer. Two windows were the case that used to show it on
# html -- the fold's guard left both standing and the pages came out with no
# <title> -- and html now writes one window per document, so the pages are
# what reaches it there.
! sngl generate --lang none --platform html --out out2 mutual.sngl
stderr 'mutual.sngl:12:20: `#a` reads its own value back through `#a`: each prop is the other, so there is nothing to answer with'

-- selfref.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"

output {
    none {
        html
    }
}

window #home(title=home.title) {
    text(value="hi")
}
-- mutual.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import nav "sngl:ui/nav"

output {
    none {
        html
    }
}

window(title=pages.current.title) {
    nav.stack #pages {
        nav.page #a(href="/a.html", title=b.title) {
            text(value="a")
        }
        nav.page #b(href="/b.html", title=a.title) {
            text(value="b")
        }
    }
}
